question: What do published routers (cost-quality cascades, learned routers) claim, and has any of the claimed cost saving been reproduced by an independent party on a different task distribution?

routers.effect_size: 98.3% inference-cost reduction while matching GPT-4 accuracy (FrugalGPT cost 0.6 vs GPT-4 cost 33.1 in paper units)
routers.baseline: best individual LLM = GPT-4 at cost 33.1 to reach the same accuracy on HEADLINES (Table 3)
routers.benchmark: HEADLINES (financial news gold-price classification; Chen et al. Table 2: 10000 examples)
routers.figure_locus: Table 3 row HEADLINES; also Figure 1(c) caption

independent_reruns.distribution: COQA / QASPER / QUALITY / MUTUAL / DIPLOMAT (not HEADLINES)
independent_reruns.result: FrugalGPT-style DistilBERT cascade reimplemented as a baseline. Mistral-7B SLM: ΔIBC -16.7 on COQA, +16.8 on DIPLOMAT, +7.7 on QASPER. Llama-2-13B SLM: ΔIBC +87.2 on QASPER. The 98.3% HEADLINES saving was not reproduced.
Independent cascade implementation beats Zero-router and individual LLMs when judge error ≤ 0.1 and degrades rapidly above 0.2. No 98% cost figure reported.

routers.notes: Figure 3 HEADLINES case study at budget $6.5 (one-fifth of GPT-4) reports 80% cost cut and +1.5% accuracy vs GPT-4 — still author-own. Table 3 also reports OVERRULING 73.3% (GPT-4 9.7 vs 2.6) and COQA 59.2% (GPT-3 72.5 vs 29.6).

routers.authors: Ong, Almahairi, Wu, Chiang, Wu, Gonzalez, Kadous, Stoica
routers.effect_size: 3.66x cost saving vs GPT-4 at CPT(50%) while holding 95% of GPT-4 quality (MT-Bench 8.8 vs GPT-4 9.3)
routers.baseline: GPT-4-only serving; equivalently random-router CPT(50%) = 49.03% (±4) GPT-4 calls (Table 1). Mixtral-8x7B is the weak model. GPT-4 $24.7/MTok vs Mixtral $0.24/MTok (Appendix D).
routers.figure_locus: Table 6 column CPT(50%) row MT Bench; Table 1 note on 8.8 vs 9.3
routers.notes: Same authors also report 1.41x on MMLU and 1.49x on GSM8K at CPT(50%) in Table 6. Different public benches, same authors — still self-reported-only under the unit rule. Figure 2 compares to Martian and Unify on MT-Bench (competitor eval, not independent replication of 3.66x).

routers.authors: Ding, Mallick, Wang, Sim, Mukherjee, Ruhle, Lakshmanan, Awadallah
routers.effect_size: 40% cost advantage (queries routed to the small model) with 0.0% BART-score drop vs all-at-large for Llama-2-7B vs Llama-2-13B (rtrans, Table 1). Abstract headline is 'up to 40% fewer calls to the large model, with no drop in response quality'.
routers.baseline: all-at-large (always the large model). Same table: 40% cost advantage with 10.3% quality drop for FLAN-T5-800M vs Llama-2-13B (large gap). Figure 1(c): 22% fewer GPT-3.5-turbo calls with <1% BART drop using Llama-2-13B as small model.
routers.benchmark: MixInstruct (Jiang et al. 2023); 10k train / 5k val / 5k test
routers.figure_locus: Table 1 (rtrans, 40% row, Llama-2 7b vs 13b and FLAN-t5 vs Llama-2-13b); Figure 1(c); abstract

independent_reruns.result: HybridLLM reimplemented as a DeBERTa baseline. ΔIBC is not the MixInstruct 40%/0-drop figure; Mistral-7B SLM HybridLLM ΔIBC +67.1 DIPLOMAT, +0.4 QASPER. Headline 40% not reproduced.

routers.notes: RouteLLM §related-work states Hybrid-LLM evaluates on MixInstruct and 'lacks evidence of out-of-domain generalization' (Ong et al. 2024).

routers.effect_size: Abstract: reducing computational cost by over 50% for comparable performance. Table 1: AutoMix+POMDP ΔIBC 151.2 on DIPLOMAT, 18.8 MUTUAL, 65.0 COQA, 114.7 QASPER, 24.1 QUALITY with Llama-2-13B as one SLM setting; DIPLOMAT average 122% ΔIBC across SLMs.
routers.baseline: SLM→LLM cost-performance curve plus reimplemented FrugalGPT and HybridLLM (0-cost verifiers at inference). ΔIBC is incremental benefit per cost vs that mix, not vs GPT-4 dollars.
routers.benchmark: QASPER, QUALITY, COQA, MUTUAL, DIPLOMAT (1000-instance validation samples; AutoMix §5 / Appendix B)
routers.figure_locus: Abstract sentence on 50% cost; Table 1 ΔIBC; Figure 4 Mistral-7B cost-quality curves
routers.notes: The 50% abstract headline is not a single Table 1 cell against a named dollar baseline; the tabled quantity is ΔIBC. Both are author-own. AutoMix is the independent rerun of FrugalGPT/HybridLLM, not an independent rerun of AutoMix.

routers.authors: Hu, Bieker, Li, Jiang, Keigwin, Ranganath, Keutzer, Upadhyay
routers.effect_size: Cascade AIQ exceeds Zero-router and individual LLMs when judge error rate ≤ 0.1; performance deteriorates rapidly when judge error exceeds 0.2. No single percent-cost-saving vs GPT-4 is reported.
routers.baseline: Zero-router and Oracle on the RouterBench cost-quality plane; individual LLMs on MMLU/MBPP/GSM8K
routers.benchmark: RouterBench MMLU, MBPP, GSM8K (Figure 5). Dataset also covers 405k precomputed inferences across eight tasks plus RAG.
routers.notes: Different authors and different tasks than FrugalGPT Table 3. This independently re-runs the cascade *class* and does not reproduce 98.3%. Predictive KNN/MLP routers in Figure 4 do not significantly beat Zero-router on several tasks.

independent_reruns.distribution: MT-Bench, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 vs mixtral-8x7b or llama-2-70b
independent_reruns.result: RouteLLM MF and causal-LLM routers, trained on Arena+judge, 'outperforming the commercial routing systems by achieving the same performance with up to 40% fewer calls routed to GPT-4.' Martian configured at $10.45/MTok max (~50% GPT-4 calls). This is a competitor measurement, not a Martian DOI/section/baseline.

routers.notes: No primary paper DOI/arXiv with a named effect size AND baseline was retrieved for Martian's own claim. Status unknown. RouteLLM Figure 2 is E3 for promoting Martian (competitor, own bench).

independent_reruns.result: Same competitor overlay as Martian. Unify configuration taken from the user dashboard 'best-performing' setting. No Unify-authored DOI/section/baseline retrieved.

routers.notes: Unknown replication status: no citable own figure with baseline.
